methodology.label: Status & scope
methodology.text: Measured results, pending owner review. Fyrr and Onyx completed the 20,000-document protocol; PipesHub’s interrupted attempt did not reach full searchable inventory, so its canonical retrieval, query latency, ingest and total cost remain n/e. This synthetic English subset has incomplete relevance labels and reduced context; it cannot establish production performance.

methodology.label: Subset derivation
methodology.text: Frozen: 250 of the core 500 questions, stratified by official type using Hamilton allocation and stable SHA-256 selection. All selected gold documents plus source-proportional distractors make 20,000 documents. 379 gold documents; 96,402,403 corpus bytes. Seed: fyrr-compare-v1-2026-11-16. The separate 10-question / 1,000-document smoke test is never a published benchmark. Exact freeze and protocol hashes are recorded below.

methodology.label: Embeddings
methodology.text: Voyage voyage-4 with 1,024 dimensions for the measured systems, using document/query input types. Native chunking, request prefixes, deduplication and caches are retained and recorded per run. Native provider-billed embedding spend is n/e where unavailable; canonical-input API cost estimates are separate.

methodology.label: Uncertainty & missing results
methodology.text: 95% percentile bootstrap intervals: 10,000 resamples, seed 1729, paired question IDs. Expected is the frozen denominator; attempted counts actual attempts; n counts valid results; missing = expected minus n, including unattempted rows. Retrieval excludes 15 empty-gold questions, leaving 235. Incomplete aggregates are partial. Unequal successful subsets cannot establish a product win.

methodology.label: Speed protocol
methodology.text: Primary: ask each of the 250 questions once per fresh service at concurrency 1 and 8, after one unrelated index warm-up. Fresh query caches; embedding-provider time included; percentile bootstrap intervals. Repeated-query warm timings remain a separate secondary track. Timed runs require a quiet host.

methodology.label: Hardware, versions & measurement date
methodology.text: Measured 17 November 2026. Native host: Intel Core i9-12900H, 14 physical cores / 20 logical CPUs, 30.576 GiB kernel-reported RAM, Linux 7.0.0-42-generic / glibc 2.43. Captured CPU, memory and kernel invariants match the native fyrr and Onyx windows. Experimental Lambda readers ran separately on AWS eu-central-1, x86_64, at 4096 or 2048 MiB. Exact commits, build/configuration hashes, phase windows and hardware-source hashes are in the JSON provenance.

methodology.label: Cost assumptions
methodology.text: Main monthly cost prices each product’s documented production deployment on AWS Frankfurt for 20,000 documents, 100,000 searches per month and 1% changed daily. Required replicas and managed services are itemized with deployment and price sources. Unknown required costs leave the total n/e, with a known subtotal shown separately. The measured single-host minimum uses matched light/C1 and team/C8 capacity references; the Lambda trial is an independent projection. These price models do not establish an AWS capacity or availability guarantee.

methodology.label: Headline wording
methodology.text: Each headline clause compares all representative products with complete measured values for that metric. n/e and partial rows cannot establish a win and are disclosed separately. Similar search quality uses at most a 2 pp gap or overlapping 95% intervals for recall@10 and nDCG@10 when both are measured; this is a descriptive rule, not an equivalence test. Faster queries require separated C1 median intervals; indexing uses accepted-document wall time. A fraction of cost requires complete stated production models and at most half the least expensive measured alternative. Overview numbers are rounded; details and JSON retain full precision.

methodology.label: Reproducibility artifacts
methodology.text: The final results reproduce from the archived retrieval scorer: 24 of 24 aggregate means and sample counts matched (n=235). The secret-checked, MIT-attributed evidence bundle is 28,432,774 bytes, above this site’s 20 MB limit. It remains in the benchmark repository pending a hosting decision; no public download URL is claimed. SHA256: 28811f50aeb45d3fcb81a51669d55374008cd213ece3e4606814d206e49e9f80.

website.variant_note: Overview: default fyrr and Onyx; PipesHub’s actual interrupted, non-default attempt is visible as unavailable. Optional details: fyrr reader.concurrency=8 on the same index, and two experimental AWS Lambda deployments of the real 20k corpus (4096 MiB and 2048 MiB). Neither changes headline wins. Lambda cold starts remain in their timings; their complete operating cost is n/e. The older 300-document synthetic trial is a separate projection. Neither real-20k Lambda deployment met the predeclared C8 latency selector; no Lambda winner is selected.

stories.title: Costs a fraction to run.
stories.description: Documented production deployments, priced on AWS Frankfurt for the same reference workload. Resources, replicas, storage, managed services and API usage are explicit. The measured single-host minimum and experimental Lambda projection stay separate.

stories.title: Answers fast.
stories.description: Median (p50) bars and p95 ticks for new and repeated questions. Lower is better. Switch between one and eight simultaneous requests.

stories.title: Indexes fast.
stories.description: Submit the same 20,000 documents to each product; time until every accepted document is searchable. Accepted and rejected counts stay visible. Lower wall time is better; setup and installation are excluded. Embedding cost is reported separately.

stories.title: Finds the right documents.
stories.description: Recall@10 measures whether the evidence your agent needs appears in its first ten documents. Higher is better.

notes: Separate synthetic 300-document trial, with deterministic in-container embeddings and a synthetic identity service. Real provider and identity latency are additional.
Warm execution and billed duration are Lambda-reported medians over 30 searches; client-observed warm latency is the varied-query median over 15 requests.
All three cold client observations are retained, including the 35.756-second outlier. Its Lambda-reported billed duration was 5.494 seconds; the additional client delay was not isolated.

The warm-only model is a billing projection. The alternative assumes 1% cold invocations, each billed for 5.494 seconds (the maximum billed duration among the three cold trials), plus 50 additional S3 reads. Neither cold fraction nor higher-volume capacity was measured.
Index storage uses the captured trial-prefix inventory: 60 objects, 1,076,222 bytes. Storage is modelled in 1,024^3-byte GB-months.
No free tier, discount or provisioned concurrency. The trial used 512 MiB ephemeral storage and reserved concurrency two; a four-request cold burst produced two successes and two throttles.
